before_taxonomy.classification_basis: Weston used identifiable photographs of Davies and later AI-manipulated depictions without her knowledge or consent to maintain the false Sophie persona. Possession of the source likeness was treated as permission to portray her, while the false identity induced intimate engagement and encounters with men who believed they knew Davies. The AI imagery supported these distinct identity and influence mechanisms, but the campaign began earlier; its consequences cannot all be attributed to AI use.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Weston used identifiable photographs of Sasha Davies from her social accounts and later made or used AI-edited/generated depictions of Davies without her knowledge or consent. The requester possessed the source likeness and treated that access as sufficient for identity-bound portrayals serving the false Sophie persona. This directly meets the person-bound requester-side recognition conditions without identifying the generator.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: AI-manipulated depictions helped maintain the false Sophie identity across social and dating accounts, inducing intimate engagement and encounters with men who believed they knew Davies.

after_taxonomy.classification_basis: Weston used identifiable photographs of Davies and later AI-manipulated depictions without her knowledge or consent to maintain the false Sophie persona. clauses.source_paraphrase: The campaign began around 2022 using Davies’s photographs for false Sophie profiles. AI-edited portrayals were used later after her accounts became private.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The ordinary-photo phase and later synthetic phase have different evidentiary scope.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The requester used Davies’s source photographs and likeness to make or deploy identity-bound AI portrayals without her knowledge or consent. The class does not require an identified generator or its internal consent decision.
The human operator selected the deceptive relationship tactic; system-side objective and instrumental choice are missing.
AI-manipulated depictions helped maintain the false Sophie identity across social and dating accounts, inducing intimate engagement and encounters with men who believed they knew Davies.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Davies reported approaches by men who believed they had chatted with her, distress and fear of leaving home. The accounts spanned social and dating platforms.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Campaign consequences are not all attributable to its undated AI phase.

clauses.source_paraphrase: She repeatedly reported accounts to platforms and police. Some accounts disappeared and were replaced; her solicitors describe limited early response.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Repeated reporting is distinct from a documented defined safeguard trigger.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: No available applicable platform protection and defined activation trigger for these specific reports are established.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Following March 2026 publicity, solicitors traced linked accounts, cross-checked a real identity and brought a High Court claim.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Identification and civil proceedings are separate from anonymous-account allegations.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 13 July, an agreed statement acknowledged wrongfulness and apologised, with £10,000 compensation and undertakings. Proposed criminal referral and promised deletion do not establish charges or verified removal.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Agreed civil remedy is distinct from a trial finding or completed enforcement.

notes: The campaign began with ordinary photos before undated AI use. No individual engagement/approach is matched to the AI phase, so the amended FC-052 no longer fails on human intent but still lacks the matched choice pathway.
